Demo controls are 40px tall, added entries can't be removed or reset, the input is overwritten with canned text after each add, and there are small dead tokens/classes and an og:image on an unsupplied host.

reason: B has the better-built system: tokens, reduced-motion handling, scroll padding, a working mobile menu with Escape and focus return, and a demo that actually shows open/handled ownership and gives the owner a real path. Its defects are local fixes: min-width:0 or overflow-wrap:anywhere on the list item, and a visible empty-state message. A is leaner and has no JS to break, but it has no phone navigation, an anchor that lands under the sticky header, and nothing to operate. I would switch to A if B's demo were judged to promise features the product doesn't have, or if the overflow bug were considered reachable in normal use.
